title: Introduction to the DOM
objective: Find elements on the page with querySelector and change their text, classes, styles and attributes
story: You've landed on Planet DOM! Everything here is a web page: headings, paragraphs, buttons. Today you'll learn to touch the page with JavaScript, that is, to change the **DOM**.

sections.title: What is the DOM?
sections.body:
When the browser opens an HTML page, it reads it and turns it into a **tree**: every tag (`h1`, `p`, `button`...) becomes an **object**. This tree is called the **DOM** (Document Object Model). JavaScript can reach these objects and change them; the moment you change them, the page changes too.

The root of the tree is the `document` object. We reach everything on the page from there.

**From today on, the tasks come with a page.** The page's HTML is given with every task; you only write the JavaScript. Create an `.html` file, put the given HTML inside `<body>`, put your code at the very bottom inside a `<script>` tag, and open the file in your browser. The code runs after the page has loaded, so all the elements are ready. `console.log` output appears in the **Console** tab of the Developer Tools. Under every page code in this book there's a screenshot showing what the page looks like when it opens.

sections.title: Finding elements with querySelector
textContent and innerHTML
sections.body: `textContent` reads or changes the **text** inside an element: ```js const status = document.querySelector("#status"); console.log(status.textContent); // the old text status.textContent = "Landing done!"; // the new text ``` `innerHTML` interprets the text you give it **as HTML**: `box.innerHTML = "Bold"` really produces bold text. **Safety note:** never put text that a user typed onto the page with `innerHTML`; someone could hide harmful HTML or code inside it. Use `textContent` to show text. That's what we'll always use in this course.

sections.title: classList, style and attributes
sections.body:
The cleanest way to change how something looks is to add or remove a **class**; CSS says what the class looks like:

```js
const panel = document.querySelector("#panel");
panel.classList.add("active");      // add
panel.classList.remove("hidden");   // remove
panel.classList.toggle("dark");     // remove if it's there, add if not
panel.classList.contains("active"); // true
```

You can also set a single style directly. Dashed CSS names become camelCase here (`background-color` → `backgroundColor`):

```js
panel.style.color = "#d63384";
panel.style.backgroundColor = "#0b1026";
```

For HTML **attributes** like `href`, `src`, `disabled`, `data-...`:

```js
const link = document.querySelector("#docs");
link.getAttribute("href");                                  // read
link.setAttribute("href", "https://developer.mozilla.org"); // change
const btn = document.querySelector("#launch");
btn.removeAttribute("disabled");                            // remove
```

challenge.title: Launch permission
challenge.prompt:
The fuel of the launch button (`#launch`) is in its `data-fuel` attribute. Write the `updateLaunch()` function:

- Read `data-fuel` with `getAttribute` and turn it into a number.
- If fuel is 50 or more: remove the button's `disabled` attribute and write `Ready for launch (fuel 80)` into `#status`.
- If it's less: put the `disabled` attribute on the button (`setAttribute("disabled", "")`) and write `Not enough fuel (fuel 30)` into `#status`.

Also set the `href` attribute of the `#docs` link to `https://developer.mozilla.org`.

project_task.title: Start screen
project_task.prompt:
Fill in the game's start screen. Write the `showStart(g)` function:

- It writes `g.title` into `#game-title`, `g.pilot` into `#pilot` and `g.level` into `#level` (`textContent`).
- It adds the `ready` class to the start button (`#start-btn`).

Don't type the texts yourself; always take them from the `g` object.
